stem: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of all living things?
explanationCorrect: Only green plants and some protists and bacteria photosynthesise. Animals and fungi don't.

explanationsWrong.B: All living cells respire to release energy.

stem: Which is the correct order of classification, from the largest group to the smallest?

options.A: Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Order, Family, Species, Genus
options.B: Phylum, Kingdom, Class, Family, Order, Genus, Species
options.C: Species, Genus, Family, Order, Class, Phylum, Kingdom
options.D: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species

explanationCorrect: Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species. (Memory aid: King Philip Came Over For Good Soup.)

explanationsWrong.A: Phylum comes before Class, and Genus before Species.
explanationsWrong.B: Kingdom is the largest group, and Order comes before Family.
explanationsWrong.C: This is smallest to largest — reversed.

stem: Which organelle is the site of aerobic respiration?
explanationCorrect: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration and release most of the cell's energy (ATP).

explanationsWrong.D: The nucleus controls the cell and holds DNA.

stem: Which structure is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
explanationCorrect: Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall (and usually chloroplasts and a large vacuole); animal cells don't.

explanationsWrong.A: Both plant and animal cells have a cell membrane.

stem: The enzyme in saliva that starts the digestion of starch is
explanationCorrect: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) breaks starch down into maltose in the mouth.

explanationsWrong.B: Pepsin digests proteins in the stomach.
explanationsWrong.D: Trypsin digests proteins in the small intestine.

stem: The raw materials for photosynthesis are
explanationCorrect: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂, using light energy absorbed by chlorophyll.

explanationsWrong.A: Oxygen and glucose are the products of photosynthesis.
explanationsWrong.B: Glucose is a product, not a raw material.

stem: Which blood vessel carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart?
explanationCorrect: The pulmonary vein is the only vein carrying oxygenated blood — from the lungs to the left atrium.

explanationsWrong.A: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs.
explanationsWrong.B: The aorta carries oxygenated blood from the heart to the body.
explanationsWrong.D: The vena cava returns deoxygenated blood from the body.

stem: During vigorous exercise, anaerobic respiration in human muscles produces
explanationCorrect: Without enough oxygen, muscle cells convert glucose to lactic acid, causing fatigue.

explanationsWrong.A: Ethanol (and CO₂) is produced by yeast, not human muscle.
explanationsWrong.C: Oxygen is used in aerobic respiration, not produced.

stem: The functional unit of the mammalian kidney is the
explanationCorrect: Each nephron filters blood and forms urine.

explanationsWrong.B: The neuron is the unit of the nervous system.
explanationsWrong.C: Alveoli are air sacs in the lungs.
explanationsWrong.D: Villi are in the small intestine, for absorption.

stem: The joint at the shoulder is an example of a
explanationCorrect: The shoulder (and hip) is a ball and socket joint, allowing movement in all directions.

explanationsWrong.A: Hinge joints (elbow, knee) move in one plane.
explanationsWrong.B: The pivot joint is between the atlas and axis vertebrae.
explanationsWrong.C: Fixed joints are found in the skull.

stem: In humans, fertilisation normally takes place in the
explanationCorrect: Sperm meets the ovum in the oviduct; the zygote then moves to the uterus to implant.

explanationsWrong.A: The uterus is where implantation and development happen.
explanationsWrong.D: Sperm is deposited in the vagina but fertilisation happens higher up.

stem: Which hormone lowers blood glucose level?
explanationCorrect: Insulin from the pancreas helps cells take up glucose and the liver store it as glycogen.

explanationsWrong.A: Adrenaline raises blood glucose for 'fight or flight'.

topicName: Ecosystems, food chains and nutrient cycles
stem: Organisms that make their own food in an ecosystem are called
explanationCorrect: Producers (autotrophs), mainly green plants, make food by photosynthesis.

explanationsWrong.D: Parasites feed on a living host.

topicName: Ecosystems, food chains and nutrient cycles
stem: As you move along a food chain from producers to top consumers, the energy available at each level
explanationCorrect: Energy is lost at each level through respiration, heat and waste — only about 10% passes on.

explanationsWrong.A: Energy can't be created; most is lost at each step.
explanationsWrong.B: Energy is lost at every transfer.

stem: Which instrument is used to estimate the population of plants in a field?
explanationCorrect: A quadrat (a square frame) is thrown randomly to count plants per unit area.

stem: Which soil type holds the most water?
explanationCorrect: Clay has the finest particles and smallest pores, so it retains the most water (and drains poorly).

explanationsWrong.A: Sandy soil has large pores and drains quickly.
explanationsWrong.C: Loam holds water moderately — ideal for most crops, but less than clay.

stem: Tallness (T) is dominant over shortness (t). What fraction of offspring of a Tt × Tt cross will be tall?
explanationCorrect: Offspring: TT, Tt, Tt, tt. Three of the four have at least one T, so 3/4 are tall.

explanationsWrong.B: 1/4 is the fraction that is short (tt).
explanationsWrong.C: 1/2 is the fraction that is heterozygous (Tt).

stem: A man of blood group AB marries a woman of blood group O. What blood groups can their children have?
explanationCorrect: The father passes A or B; the mother passes O. Children are AO (group A) or BO (group B).

explanationsWrong.A: AB needs A and B from both parents; O needs O from both.
explanationsWrong.B: Only A and B are possible here.
explanationsWrong.C: The father has no O allele to pass on.

stem: Which of these is an example of continuous variation in humans?
explanationCorrect: Height shows a range of values with no clear-cut classes — continuous variation.

explanationsWrong.A: Blood groups fall into distinct classes — discontinuous.
explanationsWrong.B: You either can or can't roll your tongue — discontinuous.

stem: The theory of use and disuse and the inheritance of acquired characters was proposed by
explanationCorrect: Lamarck proposed that organs used more develop and that acquired traits are passed on.

explanationsWrong.C: Mendel founded the laws of inheritance.

stem: Malaria is transmitted by the
explanationCorrect: Only female Anopheles mosquitoes suck blood and transmit the Plasmodium parasite.

explanationsWrong.B: Male mosquitoes feed on plant juices, not blood.
explanationsWrong.C: Houseflies spread diseases like cholera and typhoid mechanically.
